reason: The text explicitly references the Hebrews' burdens (וּבְסִבְלֹתָם - sibloṭam), which refers to their oppressive labor. Additionally, the passage describes an Egyptian striking a Hebrew man, demonstrating the pattern of violence and subjugation the Hebrews face. Moses observes both their laborious burdens and witnesses direct persecution, establishing that the Hebrews are indeed oppressed and persecuted under Egyptian rule.
